title: Ingrown toenail removal
what: The doctor removes the edge of the nail that has grown into the skin of the toe. It is usually done with local numbing.
why: When the nail edge digs into the skin, hurts, turns red, gets infected, or the ingrown nail keeps coming back.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; healing usually takes 2 to 4 weeks
tell_doctor: Diabetes and blood vessel problems in the legs
Blood thinners. Do not stop them on your own. Your doctor will decide
Allergy to numbing medicines, antibiotics, or iodine
If the nail was removed before

prepare.title: Feet
prepare.text: Wash your feet and remove nail polish.

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Bring loose, open shoes. You will have a bandage afterward.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no special prep. You can eat as normal.

steps: The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A numbing injection is given at the base of the toe
Once the toe is numb, the doctor removes the ingrown edge of the nail
Sometimes the nail root is treated so that edge does not grow back
feel: The numbing injection is unpleasant and stings for a few seconds
Then the toe goes numb, and you only feel touch
When the numbing wears off, the toe aches. A painkiller your doctor suggests helps
after: On the first day, it is best to rest more and keep your foot raised
Change the bandage as your doctor says, at home or at the clinic
Wear loose shoes for a few days
Keep the bandage dry until your doctor allows
red_flags: The toe becomes very red and swollen, or pus comes from the wound
Blood soaks through the bandage and does not stop

faq.a: Yes, usually the nail grows back, but a little narrower. The edge that was ingrown usually does not grow in again.

faq.q: Can I go to work the next day?
faq.a: If you sit at work, usually yes. If you are on your feet all day, ask your doctor about a few days of rest.

reminders.text: Ingrown toenail removal tomorrow. Remove nail polish and get loose shoes ready.
